findingDetails.title: Published report contract does not describe the emitted folder
findingDetails.evidence: The owner lists six files including benchmark-report.md; the writer and playbook contract emit seven files including skill-benchmark-report.{json,md}. The owner's Storage Shape diagram also places a run directly under benchmark/<run-label>/ while the writer lands under benchmark/reports/<run-label>.
findingDetails.claim: The owning report-storage contract and writer disagree on report filename, file count, and folder location.
findingDetails.recommendation: Choose one canonical folder shape and align all contracts, writer tests, filenames, and the storage guide.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Compared owner, playbook contract, and writer emission directly; two of three agree, the third is the declared owner.

findingDetails.title: Serving snapshots still look for a retired non-dated parity label
findingDetails.evidence: scanParityBaseline() hardcodes router-compiled-parity-baseline instead of discovering a dated archive label.
findingDetails.claim: Serving snapshots cannot discover a dated replacement for the hardcoded retired parity-baseline label.
findingDetails.recommendation: Persist or derive the dated parity-baseline label (mirror scanRealModelLast's directory scan) and update affected schema, README, and snapshot consumers.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Static lookup conflicts with the mandatory dated convention; only baseline/ is exempted. scanRealModelLast in the same file demonstrates the dated-discovery pattern is feasible here.

noveltyJustification: Traceability pass found two independent producer-consumer contract drifts after the first correctness defect: a six-versus-seven-file disagreement and a hardcoded retired parity label.

title: Published report contract does not describe the emitted folder
claim: The owning report-storage contract and writer disagree on report filename, file count, and folder location.
counterevidenceSought: Searched for any writer that emits benchmark-report.md; none exists. Searched for any consumer that reads from benchmark/<run-label>/ directly; the writer always lands under benchmark/reports/<run-label>.
alternativeExplanation: The owner's six-file benchmark-report.md contract could be a curated-only intent, but the SKILL.md does not state that separation.
downgradeTrigger: A documented separation between a raw run folder and a curated reports folder, with the writer emitting only one of them.
scopeProof: Owner, playbook, and writer disagree on one folder contract.

title: Serving snapshots still look for a retired non-dated parity label
claim: Serving snapshots cannot discover a dated replacement for the hardcoded retired parity-baseline label.
counterevidenceSought: Searched for any other caller that maps a dated archive back to the router-compiled-parity-baseline label; none exists. scanRealModelLast in the same file demonstrates the dated-discovery pattern is feasible here.
alternativeExplanation: The hardcoded label could be a frozen anchor like baseline/, but the SKILL.md only exempts baseline/ from the dated grammar; router-compiled-parity-baseline is not named as a second carve-out.
downgradeTrigger: An explicit second carve-out declared in the owning grammar for router-compiled-parity-baseline.
scopeProof: Static lookup conflicts with the mandatory dated convention; only baseline/ is exempted.
